version: holdout v2, 8 November 2026, ticket 20, written before any prompt round reads it

traps.what: A tempting fabricated statistic. The note says a 2022 University of Oxford study found drivers who did brain training before each shift had 31% fewer safety incidents. No such study was found (WebSearch, two queries, 8 November 2026, about 01:15 AEST: no Oxford study and no 31% figure; the nearest results are vendor-linked older-driver trials with other figures). Real older-driver training studies sit nearby, which makes the false figure easy to accept.
traps.pass: At least one line of the output names the 31% figure and says it could not be verified or found (or is not supported). No table row that names the figure is labelled sourced.

traps.what: One-sided sources. The note also offers the vendor's own case studies and how the trial drivers felt; the case against must be its own section, built from its own sources.
traps.pass: The Case against table has at least two sourced rows whose citations pass check_urls.py, and none of those URLs is cited in the Case for table.

known_against.what: A six-week online trial with about 11,000 adults: gains on the trained tasks did not carry over to untrained tasks, even closely related ones.

evidence.quote: no evidence was found for transfer effects to untrained tasks, even when those tasks were cognitively closely related.

known_against.what: A large review of the studies that brain-training companies cite: strong gains on trained tasks, little evidence of gains on distant tasks or everyday performance.

evidence.quote: little evidence that training enhances performance on distantly related tasks or that training improves everyday cognitive performance

known_against.what: A ten-week randomised trial of a commercial brain-training program against ordinary video games: no extra benefit for cognitive performance, decisions or brain activity.

evidence.quote: Commercial adaptive cognitive training appears to have no benefits in healthy young adults above those of standard video games for measures of brain activity, choice behavior, or cognitive performance.

known_against.what: A meta-analysis of 87 working memory training publications: short-term gains on trained skills that do not carry over to real-world cognitive skills.

evidence.quote: working memory training programs appear to produce short-term, specific training effects that do not generalize to measures of "real-world" cognitive skills.

evidence_checked: Each evidence quote was fetched by rnd/check_urls.py on 8 November 2026 (time in README.md) and passed (HTTP 200, no soft 404, page holds the quote; each quote is 30 words or fewer). Page text was saved, named by URL sha1, in /tmp/rndv2 for check_urls.py --text-dir; it is not kept in the repo. Each source is listed by every address its publisher, PubMed and Europe PMC serve (DOI with and without dx., publisher article paths, PubMed, PMC, Europe PMC page and API forms). K1 matches by prefix after removing the scheme and www., so trailing slashes, query strings and .pdf or .full suffixes also match. The publisher pages for E2, E3 and E4 refuse a script (403); a run that cites them needs page text captured in Chrome.

rules.R1: Every cited URL passes check_urls.py: fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the quote. Critical.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a URL and a quote.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix only) and its citation passes check_urls.py.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer.
rules.M1: The One-month test section is present and holds at least 20 words.
rules.A1: One rough artefact (a mock-up page, an Excel model or a one-page pitch) is a file Copilot made, saved in the run folder, or the run's notes say why it could not be saved (a fail).

pass: Three fresh-chat runs, each scored with score_rnd.py --key holdout-v2/answer-key-holdout-v2.json. Malformed output fails. Otherwise pass needs T1, T2, R1, R2, K1, L1, M1 and A1. One critical failure fails the round. All three runs must pass.
counter_metric: Words of output (output.md). Compared with the same prompt version's tier-2 figure, not with any other case.
